# K10 compiled-C2 input adapter (source-only, R2)

## What this is

A DATA-only Python (stdlib) adapter that prepares the exact inputs for executing the **already compiled** APPLIED B9 `c2.c2.mint` minting validator — the real Aiken wrapper whose `Issue` branch calls `claim.issue` — under the pinned Aiken `uplc eval --cbor` interface, with the genuine public Groth16 VK/proof payload and coherent tampered contexts. It replaces the K9 locally chosen `a2a2..` test policy with the compiled artifact's policy everywhere, so the full wrapper (singleton mint/output expects, holder check, token-name guard, VK-digest guard, and the pairing checked last) is what would run. R2 changes only the identity basis (below), the execution-proposal discipline, and documentation; the seven contexts, envelope encoding, token-name derivation and expectations are unchanged from R1.

Nothing here executes a validator. Execution needs a fresh non-author full source/effect audit that AGREEs, ordinary data generation, a fresh actual-input review, and a separate new exact bounded native AUTH (see `EXECUTION-PROPOSAL.json`).

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `tools/build_k10_inputs.py` | The adapter: pinned-input verification, independent script-hash recomputation, envelope CBOR/token-name derivation, PlutusV3 ScriptContext term generation, deterministic manifest. |
| `EXPECTATIONS.json` | Source-frozen expectations for the seven tests, the context shape, and the compiled-artifact identity with its hash basis. |
| `EXECUTION-PROPOSAL.json` | The bounded ordinary data step, the exact future native command shape, parser, budgets discipline and isolation; grants no authority. |
| `DESIGN-POSITIONS.json` | The source author's explicit positions (FOR) on every consequential clause, including the new hash basis and authority separation. |

## Generation (ordinary data step, later)

```
python3 tools/build_k10_inputs.py <b9-applied.json> <k8_fixture.ak> \
  BASE/current-cardano-k2-k10-public-inputs-generated-20261016
```

Outputs: `script.hex` (verbatim `c2.c2.mint` compiledCode), `contexts/K10-T*.uplc.txt` (one `(con data (...))` PlutusV3 ScriptContext term each), and `manifest.json`. Inputs are SHA-256-pinned and re-verified after generation; a non-empty output directory is refused. This step is stdlib-only, one attempt, zero retries, with the budgets in `EXECUTION-PROPOSAL.json`; no native AUTH is needed for the pure data step, and no hash match is claimed until root actually runs it and records a public receipt (`generated=false` until then).

## Identity: independently recomputed, tool-declared only as cross-check

The policy `6a4b67e7d46dbada1b4f49dd324018324b60b13bebbeb6f33d9d59c1` is now **independently recomputed** by the adapter from the pinned compiledCode; the `hash` field in `b9-applied.json` (echoed in `hash-c2.txt`) is used only as a cross-check, and generation fails closed if the two disagree. The generated manifest records `scriptHashClaimedHex`, `scriptHashIndependentlyRecomputedHex`, `policyIdHex` (the recomputed value) and the classification.

Source basis (exact Pallas 0.35.1 crate sources, checksum-matched per `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json`; snippets are audit citations, not runtime dependencies):

```rust
// pallas-traverse-0.35.1/src/hashes.rs:85-89
impl<const VERSION: usize> ComputeHash<28> for alonzo::PlutusScript<VERSION> {
    fn compute_hash(&self) -> Hash<28> {
        Hasher::<224>::hash_tagged(&self.0, VERSION as u8)
    }
}
// pallas-crypto-0.35.1/src/hash/hasher.rs:73-78 (Hasher<224> = Blake2b::new(28), line 59)
pub fn hash_tagged(bytes: &[u8], tag: u8) -> Hash<28> {
    hasher.input(&[tag]); hasher.input(bytes); hasher.finalize()
}
```

Aiken's side closes the loop: `compiled_code_and_hash` builds `conway::PlutusScript::<3>(program.to_cbor())` (`ast.rs:169-174`) and `Serialize` writes `compiledCode` as the hex of that same script byte slice together with its hash (`ast.rs:179-187`). Therefore, for PlutusV3:

```
recomputed = blake2b-224( 0x03 || compiledCode bytes )     # hashlib.blake2b(..., digest_size=28)
```

Before hashing, the adapter strictly decodes the compiledCode as exactly one definite CBOR byte string (`590acf` = 2767 payload bytes; shortest-form length, exact consumption, no trailing bytes, indefinite forms rejected). That decode is a structural guard only: the inner flat payload is **not** hashed, and the hash adds no second CBOR layer — neither the inner-flat preimage nor a double-CBOR preimage is correct for `hash_tagged(&self.0, 3)` as constructed above.

Audit source pins (SHA-256): pallas-traverse `hashes.rs` `eecfb1f4…6ab`, pallas-crypto `hasher.rs` `80fb9044…37e`, pallas-primitives `lib.rs` `a7c70f25…601`, pallas-primitives `plutus_data.rs` `adfebe4d…24b`, pallas-codec `utils.rs` `7019c76d…98f`, aiken `ast.rs` `d3d9009b…b27`, aiken `eval.rs` `2d63c16d…725` (full pins in `EXPECTATIONS.json` and in the generated manifest).

## Envelope CBOR cross-check

The frozen EnvV2 preimage was cross-checked against the actual Pallas `PlutusData` encoding (`pallas-primitives/src/plutus_data.rs`): `Constr` encodes its CBOR tag then its fields, and `BoundedBytes` is a single definite byte string up to 64 bytes and an indefinite 64-byte-chunk encoding above that. Every frozen envelope field is at most 32 bytes, so the definite path applies and the R1 frozen segment assembly agrees byte-for-byte; no material discrepancy was found and the encoder is unchanged (fields over 64 bytes still fail closed, unreachable here).

## Limits

The context is locally fabricated (K9 `2222../555..` fixtures, builder-chosen unbound 2030 expiry, zero fee, empty inputs) — semantically well-formed for the wrapper, but not a ledger transaction and no basis for fee, conservation, admission, wallet, signing or Preprod claims; it must never be presented as a live Preprod claim. The single-party Class-0 setup could forge proofs and the VK-matrix link is unproved; all broader obligations (20 UTxO families, ACTUS/DeFi and general obligations, recursion, private handoff, bounded multi-parent PCD, universal certificates, real Preprod) remain open.

report:
# K10 R2 primary-hash input adapter — source author result

## Verdict

The R2 five-file source is complete as a **source proposal ready for a fresh non-author full source/effect audit**, and for nothing stronger. It adds the one missing R1 capability — actual independent public C2 script-hash recomputation grounded in the exact Pallas 0.35.1 sources — while preserving R1 context, envelope, token-name and seven-test behavior. Nothing was executed or generated by this author (`generated=false`); no hash match is reported as observed, no fresh review vote is fabricated, and no authority is granted.

First blocked boundary: **fresh non-author audit (must AGREE) → root ordinary data generation observing the hash assert**. All native, ledger and Preprod boundaries remain behind it.

## The hash algorithm, source-grounded

- `pallas-traverse/src/hashes.rs:85-89`: `ComputeHash<28> for PlutusScript<VERSION>` is `Hasher::<224>::hash_tagged(&self.0, VERSION as u8)`; for V3 the tag is the single raw byte `0x03`.
- `pallas-crypto/src/hash/hasher.rs:59,73-78`: `Hasher<224>` is Blake2b with a 28-byte digest; `hash_tagged` inputs `&[tag]` then the slice, adding no CBOR encoding (contrast NativeScript `hash_tagged_cbor`, hashes.rs:73-76).
- `pallas-primitives/src/lib.rs:186-196`: `PlutusScript<VERSION>` is a transparent `Bytes`; `PolicyId = Hash<28>`. Aiken `ast.rs:151-187` builds `conway::PlutusScript::<3>(program.to_cbor())` and serializes `compiledCode` as hex of **that same byte slice** with its hash — so the compiledCode slice (2770B, `590acf…`, b9-applied.json:22-23) is the hashed slice.

Hence R2 computes `blake2b-224(0x03 || compiledCode bytes)` via `hashlib.blake2b(..., digest_size=28)`, after a strict guard decoding the compiledCode as exactly one definite CBOR byte string (shortest-form length, exact consumption, no trailing bytes; 2767B inner flat payload). The inner flat payload is **not** hashed and no double-CBOR re-wrap is hashed; the artifact-declared hash `6a4b67e7…59c1` is only a pinned cross-check, and generation fails closed on disagreement. The generated manifest will record claimed, independently recomputed, and classification; Pallas/Aiken SHA-256 pins are audit citations there, not runtime dependencies.

## Envelope cross-check

`pallas-primitives/src/plutus_data.rs:348-371,423-443` (Constr tag+fields; BoundedBytes definite ≤64B, indefinite 64B chunks above) agrees with the R1 frozen EnvV2 preimage on every frozen field (all ≤32B). No material discrepancy was found, so the encoder is unchanged and >64B still fails closed — a deliberate minimal R2, not a restyle.

## Exact changed-lines map (R1 → R2)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tools/build_k10_inputs.py` | Docstring identity paragraphs replaced (R1:16-20); new constants `INNER_FLAT_LEN/PLUTUS_V3_TAG/SCRIPT_HASH_BYTES/AUDIT_SOURCE_PINS` after R1:44; new `blake2b224`, `decode_single_cbor_bytes`, `recompute_script_hash` after R1:61; Pallas citation comment added above `_cbor_head` (R1:87) with no encoder change; `extract_compiled` (R1:274-295) now returns `(code_hex, recomputed_hex)` and asserts recomputed == declared; `main` policy source (R1:320) now `bytes.fromhex(recomputed_hash)`; manifest (R1:368-391) gains `scriptInnerFlatBytes`, `scriptHashClaimedHex`, `scriptHashIndependentlyRecomputedHex`, classification/preimage/algorithm and `auditSourcePins`, and limitation 3 reworded. All other R1 lines (Data model, CBOR/UPLC encoders, envelope, frozen preimage, context builder, fixture extraction, seven cases, pin before/after) are preserved. |
| `EXPECTATIONS.json` | Format bumped to `/2` with `generated:false`; `compiledArtifact` gains inner-flat size, claimed/recomputed fields and new classification; new top-level `scriptHash` object (algorithm, guard, primary basis, archive receipts, seven audit pins); `positiveEnvelope.pallasPlutusDataCrosscheck` added; context/redeemer/scriptInfo wording records recomputed policy; seven test objects unchanged. |

No other party's vote is stated. |

## Preserved R1 behavior

Seven source predicates remain: T1 genuine accept; T2 N1 body / T3 N2 context coherent envelope+name+mint+output rebuilds refused by the pairing; T4 N3 A/C swap (+3-quantity semantics unchanged in T5 qty=2, T6 name bitflip, T7 VK-digest bitflip structural refusals at their named guards). The raw 16-field V3 context, Issue redeemer and Minting script-info use the actual mint wrapper — not a typed unit/Bool consumer. Chosen outref `2222…`/claimant `555…`, zero fee and 2030 expiry remain **LOCAL FABRICATED**, never a live Preprod claim. No geometry/curve/offchain verifier was added; the public payload stays static only.

## Scope, limitations, independence

This author acted only as fallback source author in an independent new context, read only the exact public mirror (original paths mapped through INPUT-INDEX.json), and executed nothing — no shell/Python/native/Aiken/curve/RNG/setup/proof/key/wallet/network/signing/ledger action and no nested agents. The fallback confirmation (nativeExecutionAuthorityCreated=false) is authorship routing, not approval. Class-0 forgeability, the VK-matrix binding, all 20 UTxO families, ACTUS/DeFi/general obligations, real recursion, private handoff, bounded multi-parent PCD, universal certificates and actual Preprod remain open; no percentage of full compatibility is claimed. A future actual Cardano ledger step would need a real proof context binding a new funded wallet and an actual settle outref under a reviewed prover by a private operator — not a root key read, and no partial wallet authorization or runtime calls exist here.

## Unread inputs and unresolved evidence

Unread: every INPUT-INDEX entry not listed in coverage.readPaths (notably the full DATA-ONLY manifest body, most uplc/Pallas/stdlib/K8/K9 bodies outside cited windows, b9 validators beyond the c2 titles, and Pallas test_data, which is absent from the crate archives). Unresolved: (1) the hash identity is a proposed assert expected from source, unobserved until root generation; (2) the `Program::to_cbor/from_cbor` implementation file is not separately indexed — R2 rests on the indexed ast.rs call sites, Serialize deduction, eval.rs `from_cbor` usage and the transparent-Bytes CBOR definitions, which the fresh audit should confirm directly; (3) Pallas hash test vectors are not in the archives, so no third-party vector cross-check was possible in-mirror; (4) native acceptance/refusal at the named guards, ledger ExUnits/fees and any Preprod property remain entirely unobserved.
